answer_quotes: Probably first year – first year of secondary school. Year 7, because the teachers were nice to me.

I got my highest GCSE in DT and ‘cos I chose my ‘A’ levels through my highest subjects at GCSE, because I loved science but at the same time I liked English and the arts as well and if I did science all day I’d get bored, if I did art all day I’d get bored, so DT’s a nice crossover
Lots – they tried to persuade me against it.

They said that I had a good er I would say RSA qualification and I had good communication skills and I got an A at ‘A’ levels in my English, so I should do journalism or management and work in an office environment but I just didn’t want to do that.
one of the girls had done industrial design technology and had come out and found a really, really good job and she was a car designer now – it was wonderful
my mum suddenly became very feminist and she said you can do anything, don’t end up like your dad and so I’ve always had it drummed into me, confidence and things like that
the course is a lot more competitive than I expected it to be and it’s the nasty level, and there are really, really, really nasty people who do not want you to succeed
everyone’s competing with everybody
in practice no, I hate group work
they’ve managed to position our deadlines perfectly so we’ve got phys – like deadlines, during revision week and during exam week because we don’t have a revision week
He’s wicked – he really is. … I really feel that he looks out for me.
I love it to bits and I wouldn’t change it but I do have a love/hate relationship with the department
seeing placement basically as a taster and to try and work out – even if I hate what I do for a year, at least I can rule that out
to earn a bit, as well
mentally I’m feeling old enough and I want the responsibility, I want to get out of the {D&T building] and live life and be able to watch evening television
if I found a job I love, on placement, I’m gonna work my absolute the hardest to try and get that job afterwards
the equality, or the sense of equality I should say, really appeals. And not having to try and establish yourself, in your own right, because you’re a woman
placement tutor is about as much use as a chocolate teapot at the moment

I’d like to work for a large company or a large consultancy such as [company]. Because [company] are Italian, all male, and I’m English and I’m female and this seems like a really good place to try and crack.
working for a consultancy, building up my CV, paying off my student loan – that’s where I’ll be in 5 years time
settled down, probably marriage wise – because that is quite important to me, but my career will probably come first
I might set up my own consultancy, in London, and employ female designers – only
the location as well does come into it, because I want to go back towards home home
I never want to feel financially dependent on a man.
